requirements.original: lengthof(in template (present) any inpar) return integer
requirements.canonical: The `lengthof` predefined function has the signature lengthof(in template (present) any inpar) return integer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.2.1 -- lengthof(in template (present) any inpar) return integer

requirements.original: This function returns the length of a value or template that is of type bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of, array or map. The units of length for each
requirements.canonical: The `lengthof` function SHALL return the length of a value or template of type bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of, array or map.

examples.text:
lengthof(charstring : "HELLO")  // returns 5 
  lengthof(octetstring : ('12'O, '34'O)) // returns 1 
  lengthof('1??1'B)  // returns 4 
  lengthof(universal charstring : ? length(8)) // returns 8 
  lengthof('1*F'H)   // shall cause an error 
  lengthof('1*F'H length (8))  // returns 8
  lengthof(bitstring : ? length(2..infinity)) // shall cause an error 
  lengthof('00*FF'O length(1..2))    // returns 2 
  lengthof('1*49'H length(1..2))    // shall cause an error 
  lengthof('1'B length(3))  // shall cause an error 
  lengthof('1*1'B length(10..20))    // shall cause an error

requirements.original: For values or templates of record `of or set` `of type, the value to be returned is the maximum of the minimal length` restriction value of the type, or 0 for types with no minimal length restriction, and the index of the last initialized element plus 1.
requirements.canonical: For a value or template of a record of or set of type, `lengthof` SHALL return the maximum of (a) the minimal length restriction value of the type, or 0 if the type has no minimal length restriction, and (b) the index of the last initialized element plus 1.
requirements.condition: inpar is of a record of or set of type
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.2.1 -- For values or templates of record `of or set` `of type, the value to be returned is the maximum of the minimal length` restriction value of the type, or 0 for types with no minimal length restriction, and the index of the last initialized element plus 1.

requirements.original: When the function lengthof is applied to templates of record of or set of types, inpar shall only contain the following matching mechanisms: specific value, value list, complemented value list, "?" requirements.canonical: When `lengthof` is applied to a template of a record of or set of type, `inpar` SHALL only contain the matching mechanisms specific value, template list, complemented template list, "?" (AnyValue), "*" (AnyValueOrNone), SuperSet, SubSet, combined template, permutation and the length restriction matching attribute.
requirements.condition: inpar is a record of or set of template

ambiguity.issue: Clauses B.1.2.1 and B.1.2.2 name these matching mechanisms 'template list' and 'complemented template list'.

examples.text:

  template RoI mw_roI1 := { 1, permutation(2, 3), ? } 
  template RoI mw_roI2 := {1, *, (2, 3) } 
  template RoI mw_roI3 := { 1, *, 10 } length(5) 
  template RoI mw_roI4 := { 1, 2, 3, * } length(1..2) 
  template RoI mw_roI5 := { 1, 2, 3, * } length(1..3) 
  lengthof (mw_roI1) // returns 4 
  lengthof (mw_roI2) // shall cause an error 
  lengthof (mw_roI3) // returns 5 
  lengthof (mw_roI4) // shall cause an error 
  lengthof (mw_roI5) // returns 3

requirements.original: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is matching a specific value (clause B.1.1), a matching mechanism instead of values (clause B.1.2) or matching character pattern (clause B.1.5), the function shall return true if the content of the invalue parameter is of the same kind.
requirements.canonical: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is specific value (B.1.1), a matching mechanism instead of values (B.1.2) or matching character pattern (B.1.5), `istemplatekind` SHALL return true if the content of `invalue` is of the same kind.
requirements.condition: kind denotes specific value, a matching mechanism instead of values or a matching character pattern
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.3.5 -- If the matching mechanism kind enquired is matching a specific value (clause B.1.1), a matching mechanism instead of values (clause B.1.2) or matching character pattern (clause B.1.5), the function shall return true if the content of the invalue parameter is of the same kind.

requirements.original: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is a matching mechanism inside values (clause B.1.3), the function shall return true if the template in the invalue parameter contains this kind of matching mechanism on the first level of nesting.
requirements.canonical: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is a matching mechanism inside values (B.1.3), `istemplatekind` SHALL return true if the template in `invalue` contains this kind of matching mechanism on the first level of nesting.
requirements.condition: kind denotes a matching mechanism inside values
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.3.5 -- If the matching mechanism kind enquired is a matching mechanism inside values (clause B.1.3), the function shall return true if the template in the invalue parameter contains this kind of matching mechanism on the first level of nesting.

requirements.original: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is a matching attribute (clause B.1.4), the function shall return true if the template in the invalue parameter has this kind of matching attribute attached to it directly (i.e. it doesn't count if the attribute is attached to a field of invalue at any level of nesting).
requirements.canonical: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is a matching attribute (B.1.4), `istemplatekind` SHALL return true only if the template in `invalue` has this kind of matching attribute attached to it directly, not to a field of `invalue` at any level of nesting.
requirements.condition: kind denotes a matching attribute
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.3.5 -- If the matching mechanism kind enquired is a matching attribute (clause B.1.4), the function shall return true if the template in the invalue parameter has this kind of matching attribute attached to it directly (i.e. it doesn't count if the attribute is attached to a field of invalue at any level of nesting).

requirements.original: In all other cases the function returns false.
requirements.canonical: In all cases not covered by the rules for specific values, matching mechanisms instead of values, patterns, matching mechanisms inside values and matching attributes, `istemplatekind` SHALL return false.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.3.5 -- In all other cases the function returns false.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.3.5 -- In addition to the general error causes given in clause 16.1.2, the following restrictions apply:

requirements.original: a) Calling the istemplatekind function with a different second parameter than stated in table C.1 shall lead to an error.
requirements.canonical: Calling `istemplatekind` with a `kind` argument that is not one of the values stated in table C.1 SHALL lead to an error.
requirements.condition: kind is not one of the values of table C.1
